chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who purchased from a man with a dinar, so he took half as goods and half as silver (dirhams). He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

And I asked him: 'Is it permissible that he takes half as silver or goods, and leaves the other half until he comes later and takes it as silver or goods?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he leaves anything from it until he takes it all, so he should not do it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on splitting a gold dinar payment into silver and goods in Islamic finance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the permissibility (jawaz) of immediate mixed settlement and the preferred practice (istihbab) of avoiding deferred exchange to prevent riba al-fadl. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on eliminating uncertainty (gharar) and delay in currency swaps, ensuring that the exchange is complete and simultaneous to maintain the integrity of the transaction.
